editorial.headline: Craft Goods That Are Nationally Open, But Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32903 covers plant, animal, floral and shell-based craft manufacturing, open nationally to all business scales but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 32903 is a manufacturing code for craft goods that sit outside a narrower named category.** The record describes the making of handicraft items from plant and animal materials: coconut tree products, shells, coconut fibre, roots, leather, ivory, horn, bone, feathers and hair. It also includes preserved animals and taxidermy, wreaths, circular flower arrangements and flower baskets, as well as artificial flowers, fruits and leaves. The scope extends to painted craft goods and to craft items made from fish skin and shells, including pearl oyster shell such as *Pinctada maxima*, mabe shell and other shells.

That breadth matters because this is not only a souvenir label or a retail-facing craft identity. It is an industrial activity code for making the objects themselves. A registrant using this code is identifying the production of craft goods from the materials named in the record, including natural plant materials, animal-derived materials, preserved forms, floral arrangements, artificial botanical objects and shell-based work. The scale field is unusually broad: the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In plain English, the record allows the code to be used across the full business-scale range, from micro operators to large-scale businesses, provided the registered activity stays inside this described manufacturing scope.

Nationally, the investment picture looks open. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The source named for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, a foreign-owned company is not capped below full ownership for this activity. That is the clean national rule in the slim record: open status, 100% maximum foreign ownership, and availability across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales.

Bali is the decisive exception. The record marks this code as blocked for Bali PMA registration: l4_bali_blocked is true and the Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, blocked by the Bali moratorium in May 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is direct. KBLI 32903 is nationally foreign-open up to 100%, but a foreigner cannot register it in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
